title: X.509 CRL Structure
description: Builds and parses X.509 certificate revocation lists with revoked serials, reasons, and signatures. The CA signs the list; verifiers download it on schedule. It is the classic revocation mechanism.

demo.title: Demo — X.509 CRL Structure

title: Delta CRLs
description: Publishes delta CRLs with only new revocations since the last full list. Clients combine base plus deltas; downloads shrink dramatically. It keeps CRLs practical at scale.

demo.title: Demo — Delta CRLs

title: OCSP Checking
description: Queries OCSP responders for real-time revocation status per certificate. Fresh answers beat stale lists; responders sign the status. Privacy and availability are the tradeoffs.

demo.title: Demo — OCSP Checking

title: OCSP Stapling
description: Staples the OCSP response to the TLS handshake so clients get freshness free. The server fetches and caches the response; clients verify without extra connections. It fixes OCSP's privacy and latency problems.

demo.title: Demo — OCSP Stapling

title: CRLite Compression
description: Compresses the web's revocations into CRLite filters browsers download efficiently. Bloom-filter cascades encode millions of revocations in megabytes. Firefox proved it at scale.

demo.title: Demo — CRLite Compression

title: Distribution Points
description: Partitions revocation by CRL distribution points in certificates. Each cert points to its CRL; verifiers fetch only relevant lists. It scales revocation checking.

demo.title: Demo — Distribution Points

title: Revocation Checking Policies
description: Defines when verifiers require fresh revocation data versus soft-fail. Hard-fail is safer but breaks on responder outages; policies encode the tradeoff. Each application picks deliberately.

demo.title: Demo — Revocation Checking Policies

title: Timestamping (RFC 3161)
description: Timestamps signatures so they validate even after the cert expires or revokes. The TSA's signed timestamp proves the signature existed while the cert was good. Long-lived code signatures depend on it.

demo.title: Demo — Timestamping (RFC 3161)

title: CA/Browser Forum Rules
description: Follows CA/Browser Forum baseline requirements for revocation timelines. Compromised certs must revoke within days; the rules are audited. It sets the industry's minimum bar.

demo.title: Demo — CA/Browser Forum Rules

title: Key Compromise Response
description: Executes the key-compromise playbook: revoke, replace, notify, investigate. Speed matters; the playbook is rehearsed before it is needed. It turns panic into procedure.

demo.title: Demo — Key Compromise Response

title: ACME Revocation Automation
description: Automates issuance and revocation with ACME. Certificates live 90 days; revocation is an API call. Automation makes short lifetimes and fast revocation practical.

demo.title: Demo — ACME Revocation Automation

title: Certificate Transparency
description: Logs all certificates in public transparency logs so misissuance is visible. Monitors watch for unauthorized certs; browsers require SCTs. It makes the PKI auditable.

demo.title: Demo — Certificate Transparency

title: CRL Caching Strategy
description: Caches CRLs with nextUpdate-aware refresh to balance freshness and load. Clients reuse lists until they expire; servers set sensible lifetimes. It keeps revocation checking cheap.

demo.title: Demo — CRL Caching Strategy

title: Fail-Open vs Fail-Closed
description: Decides the failure mode when revocation data is unreachable. Fail-closed is safer; fail-open keeps working. The decision encodes risk appetite per application.

demo.title: Demo — Fail-Open vs Fail-Closed

title: Sigstore Transparency
description: Signs software with Sigstore's transparency-backed short-lived certificates. Rekor logs every signature; Fulcio issues ephemeral certs. It brings CT-style transparency to code signing.

demo.title: Demo — Sigstore Transparency
